common_name: Butterscotch Baby Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Golden Red-Edged Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Butterscotch Baby, part of the patented Chick Charms series, opens a 4-6 inch rosette of fleshy butterscotch-orange leaves rimmed in bright red that deepen through the season into burnt caramel and finally a frosted purple-black as winter cold sets in. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, since strong light is what drives the clearest gold-to-amber color progression. A thick stalk of starry pink flowers rises from mature rosettes in summer before that rosette dies back, leaving the offsets it has already produced on short stolons to carry the clump forward. As with other sempervivums, winter wet is the real threat, not cold, so sharp drainage matters more than soil fertility.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Bing Cherry Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Cherry-Red Velvet Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Bing Cherry, the Chick Charms trade name for the cultivar 'Aglow', forms a large velvety rosette up to 8 inches across that reads deep cherry-wine in cool weather, shifts toward burnt orange as summer heat builds, then picks up a tawny green sheen in fall while still holding red undertones. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, where bright light keeps the velvet-textured leaves from washing out to plain green. It is a prolific offsetter, throwing new chicks on short stolons every spring to bulk up a planting quickly, and like other hens and chicks it needs protection from standing winter water far more than from cold.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Cotton Candy Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Cobweb Sempervivum)

planting.note: Tuck offsets into shallow pockets of very well-drained, lean, gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Cotton Candy, the Chick Charms trade name for the cobweb houseleek selection 'Emily', has small, tightly packed rosettes in green shading to burgundy, each tip laced in the fine silvery-white webbing that gives the whole species its common name. Tuck offsets into shallow pockets of very well-drained, lean, gravelly soil in full sun, where the webbing develops most densely and the burgundy tones intensify. Starry pink-and-white flowers appear on short stalks in midsummer above the rosettes that are about to flower and die, while surrounding offsets knit together into an expanding low mat. It is extremely cold-hardy and best suited to rock gardens, troughs, and crevices where its diminutive scale and cobweb detail can be seen up close.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide
British Cactus and Succulent Society reference

common_name: Sugar Shimmer Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Silver-Haired Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Sugar Shimmer, part of the patented Chick Charms series, forms a tightly packed rosette in pale blue-green with soft pink tips, the whole surface dusted in fine silver-white hairs that catch the light like spun sugar. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun to light shade, since strong light keeps the hairs dense and the pink margins from fading; those margins deepen toward lavender as temperatures drop through fall and winter. It produces a steady supply of new chicks on short stolons around the central hen, and like other sempervivums it tolerates hard freezes far better than wet winter soil.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Autumn Apple Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Olive-and-Apple-Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Autumn Apple builds a large rosette, up to 8 inches across at maturity, of olive-green leaves margined in candy-apple red, with the red band widening and intensifying as nights cool into fall and winter. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, where bright light pushes the red margin darker and keeps the center from staying plain green. It is a vigorous grower that fills in quickly from offsets, making it useful for covering ground in a rock garden or raised bed within a season or two, and it needs the same sharp winter drainage that all hardy sempervivums depend on to avoid rot.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Plum Parfait Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Plum-Purple Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Plum Parfait, the Chick Charms trade name for the Kevin Vaughn-bred cultivar 'Prairie Sunset', opens each 3-4 inch rosette in soft yellow-green touched with pink, then deepens through the growing season into a rich plum-purple with just a hint of green showing through at the base of the leaves. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, since the purple tones are most saturated under strong light and fade toward green in shade. A thick stalk of pink, star-shaped flowers appears on mature rosettes in summer, and the clump continues on from offsets after that rosette flowers and dies. Give it the same sharp drainage every sempervivum needs, since winter wet rather than cold is what causes losses.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Mint Marvel Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Blue-Green Wine-Tipped Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of well-drained, ideally slightly alkaline gritty soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Mint Marvel is a selection of the lime-loving houseleek species prized for its large blue-green rosette tipped in rich burgundy-wine at each leaf point, a contrast that sharpens with cooler temperatures and strong sun. Press offsets onto the surface of well-drained, ideally slightly alkaline gritty soil in full sun, keeping in mind that calcareum selections tolerate a damp winter somewhat better than most other sempervivums while still needing sharp drainage overall. It offsets readily on stolons to form a spreading clump, and the wine-colored tips fade toward plain blue-green if the plant is grown in too much shade.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Gold Mine Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Giants Golden Red-Blushed Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Gold Mine is one of the oversized Giants-series Chick Charms selections, opening lime-green in spring before maturing into a golden-yellow rosette with a burgundy-red blush that deepens toward the center. At 9-12 inches across it is noticeably larger than most hens and chicks, a scale bred into the Giants line to stand out in mixed container plantings. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, where strong light intensifies both the gold base color and the red center blush. It is a plant patent variety, so propagate it for personal garden use only; like other sempervivums it needs sharp winter drainage far more than protection from cold.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Pink Sapphire Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Giants Rose-Centered Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Pink Sapphire is a Giants-series selection built around a single oversized rosette, up to 10 inches across, with a dark rose-pink center fading through a narrow transition zone to a fine light-green margin. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, where strong light keeps the pink center saturated rather than washing out to green. As with other Giants selections, the scale makes it a good anchor plant in a mixed trough or container planting of smaller sempervivums, though it still offsets into new chicks that can be separated and grown on. Give it the same sharp drainage every sempervivum needs, since cold is rarely the limiting factor compared with wet winter soil.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Steel Appeal Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Giants Steel-Blue Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall.

directions: Steel Appeal is a large Giants-series rosette, reaching around 10 inches across, in steel-blue-grey with a hot pink to garnet-red center and fine silvery cilia lining the leaf margins. Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun, since strong light is what keeps the steely blue tone and red center from fading to plain green. The amount of red at the leaf base shifts with the season, deepening in cool weather and receding somewhat in summer heat. It is sold as a plant patent variety, so divisions should stay in personal garden use, and like other sempervivums it needs protection from standing winter water far more than from cold.
sources: Mountain Crest Gardens — Sempervivum Cultivar Guide

common_name: Jolly Green Aeonium (Spreading Green Saucer-Rosette Aeonium)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in fast-draining succulent mix after callusing; grow in full sun to light shade in mild coastal climates.

directions: Jolly Green arose as a chance seedling in a California succulent collector's garden and forms dense clusters of long, pointed green rosettes on low, horizontally spreading stems, staying under a foot tall while eventually covering several feet of ground. Clusters of small yellow flowers appear on mature rosettes. Grow in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix in full sun along the mild coast or light afternoon shade in hotter inland gardens, watering through the cool growing season and letting the soil dry out in summer dormancy when rot risk is highest. Because it spreads horizontally rather than building a tall branching trunk like tree aeoniums, it works well as a textured groundcover or cascading over a wall in frost-free gardens.
